the_trade_off_made: We favoured immediate business impact and legal risk over pure revenue and fairness scores. This pushes a high‑paying Enterprise customer (NEW-00001) behind the payment failure, and a free‑plan security alert ahead of the legal request. The cost is a slight delay for the Enterprise demo and a perception of unfairness for the paying customer.
hardest_call: Placing the security incident (NEW-00004) ahead of the legal GDPR request (NEW-00002) was hardest, because both have policy lifts and overdue status, and one could argue legal compliance should outrank a suspected breach.

how_it_ranked_the_four_ways.why_it_ranks_here: Business impact (users affected, work blocked) directly determines revenue loss and customer trust, which we prioritized.
how_it_ranked_the_four_ways.what_it_gets_wrong: It can undervalue high‑paying customers whose issues have lower immediate impact.

how_it_ranked_the_four_ways.why_it_ranks_here: Legal and overdue tickets carry penalties and SLA breaches, so timing is the next priority.
how_it_ranked_the_four_ways.what_it_gets_wrong: Deadlines may push less damaging but time‑sensitive tickets ahead of higher‑impact problems.

how_it_ranked_the_four_ways.why_it_ranks_here: Revenue is important but secondary to preventing large‑scale outages or legal breaches.
how_it_ranked_the_four_ways.what_it_gets_wrong: It can unfairly deprioritise free‑plan users with serious issues.

how_it_ranked_the_four_ways.why_it_ranks_here: Ensuring equal treatment is valuable but was outweighed by impact, legal risk, and revenue considerations.
how_it_ranked_the_four_ways.what_it_gets_wrong: Relying on fairness alone could ignore critical business or compliance risks.

why_the_winner_beat_the_runner_up: Damage outranked deadline because the payment failure halted revenue for thousands, whereas the legal request, while important, affected only one user and had more time before the SLA expires.
